concept.name: Permanent market impact
concept.definition: The component of market impact that persists after trading ends, attributed to the information other participants infer from the order flow: the market re-prices the asset because trading itself signals that someone wants to buy or sell in size. It reflects adverse-selection and information content rather than transient liquidity demand.
concept.intuition: The market learns from your footprint: once participants believe a big informed buyer is active, the price stays higher even after you finish.
concept.mechanics: Each trade updates other participants' beliefs about fundamental value or about the existence of a large latent order; quotes re-level and do not revert. In Kyle-style models this is the linear, information-driven response of price to signed order flow (Kyle's lambda).
concept.formula: Kyle's lambda: price change = lambda x signed order flow, estimated as the regression coefficient of price changes on trade size over a window.
concept.failure_modes: Permanent impact is invisible in real time - you only infer it from non-reversion, so execution algorithms can systematically underestimate it for informative flow. It also punishes predictable scheduling: the more detectable the pattern, the larger the inferred information content.
concept.misconceptions: Large trades do not have permanent impact only when the trader is informed - the market cannot distinguish intent, so even uninformed size moves expectations. And impact being 'permanent' does not mean the price never moves again for other reasons.
concept.example: After a fund accumulates 5% of a small-cap over two weeks, the price settles 8% higher and stays there: the market has priced in the persistent demand it detected.
